title: Phase compositions of Si oxynitride: A comprehensive thermodynamic modeling study
authors: Andrey Sarikov, Mariia Babiichuk, Mariia Voitovych, Sergii V. Mamykin1
abstract: In this work, a comprehensive thermodynamic description of the formation of phases in amorphous SiOxNy (0 <= x <= 2, 0 <= y <= 4/3) films as a function of the film chemical composition and fabrication temperature is presented. Two possible phase states, namely homogeneous single-phase Si oxynitride and two-phase mixture of Si oxide and Si nitride phases, are analyzed in terms of the lowest values of the Gibbs free energy. The characters of the modification of the phase composition upon changing the SiOxNy stoichiometry indices and fabrication temperature are determined. Moreover, characteristic features of the chemical composition of the Si oxide and Si nitride phases in two-phase Si oxynitrides are revealed. Particular attention is given to the thermodynamic origin of the boundaries between different phase states of the SiOxNy films and to determining the critical stoichiometry values separating them. A comprehensive phase diagram indicating single- and two-phase SiOxNy regions as functions of the fabrication temperature is constructed. The peculiarities of the transitions between different SiOxNy phase states, along with underlying mechanisms, are discussed with reference to this phase diagram. The obtained results extend our understanding of the fundamental properties of Si oxynitride films and their dependence on the film fabrication conditions, and may be used for tailoring SiOxNy characteristics for practical applications.
summary: This work presents a comprehensive thermodynamic model to predict the stable phase composition of amorphous SiOxNy films. By minimizing the Gibbs free energy, the authors distinguish between single-phase and two-phase states across varying stoichiometry and temperature. The resulting phase diagram provides a predictive tool for tailoring the material's properties for practical applications.
main_problem: To provide a comprehensive thermodynamic description of the phase formation in amorphous SiOxNy films as a function of chemical composition and fabrication temperature.
main_result: The study constructs a phase diagram showing single- and two-phase SiOxNy regions, determining the stable phase by minimizing the Gibbs free energy.
method: Thermodynamic modeling based on comparing the Gibbs free energy of homogeneous versus two-phase mixtures.
model_or_system: The system is amorphous SiOxNy films, analyzed using the Random Bonding Model (RBM) to describe local structures in both single-phase and two-phase states.
key_observables: Gibbs free energy (G), phase composition (single-phase vs. two-phase), and critical stoichiometry values.
important_parameters: Film chemical composition (SiOxNy stoichiometry indices) and fabrication temperature (T).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares the Gibbs free energy of a single-phase state against the minimum Gibbs free energy of a two-phase mixture of Si oxide and Si nitride.
figures_summary: A comprehensive phase diagram is constructed illustrating the single- and two-phase SiOxNy regions as a function of fabrication temperature.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the thermodynamic stability by comparing the Gibbs free energy for homogeneous versus heterogeneous (two-phase) states across the entire stoichiometry range, leading to the construction of the phase diagram.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science, the core methodology—using Gibbs free energy minimization to predict phase transitions based on composition and temperature—is a fundamental concept in statistical mechanics applicable to many complex many-body systems.
